question: When studying the human body, what does anatomy focus on?

options.A: The physical structure of body parts

explanation: Spot on! Anatomy is all about the physical setup—the shapes, forms, and structures of body parts. Think of it as learning the map of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: How do anatomy (structure) and physiology (function) work together in patient care?

options.A: Structure always determines the function of body parts
options.B: They are completely separate systems with no overlap
options.C: Function dictates how physical structures will grow
options.D: Physiology is studied only when anatomy is abnormal

explanation: You got it! How a body part is built (anatomy) directly decides what it can do (physiology). For example, the heart's muscular walls are shaped precisely to pump blood! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: What do we call a group of similar cells working together to do a specific job?
explanation: Great job! Tissues are formed when team-player cells group up to share a specific duty in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: Your stomach is an organ. What is it primarily made of?

options.D: A single type of specialized cell

explanation: Spot on! An organ isn't just made of one thing; it teams up different tissue types (like muscle and lining tissues) to handle big jobs like digestion. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the term for all the chemical reactions happening inside your body cells?
explanation: You nailed it! Metabolism is the grand total of all building-up and breaking-down reactions keeping your cells alive and kicking. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which life process helps your body quickly react to changes around you, like pulling your hand from a hot surface?
explanation: Correct! Responsiveness is your body's way of detecting changes in the environment and reacting fast to keep you safe. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: In standard anatomical position, how are a person's palms facing?
explanation: Spot on! In the standard anatomical position, the body stands upright with palms facing forward. It's our universal reference point in healthcare. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which body plane cuts the body into top (superior) and bottom (inferior) portions?
explanation: You got it! A transverse plane slices horizontally, dividing the body neatly into upper and lower halves. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which specific body cavity safely houses the spinal cord?
explanation: Spot on! The vertebral canal runs right down your backbone to protect your precious spinal cord. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of the slippery fluid found between serous membrane layers around organs?

options.A: To reduce friction between moving organs
options.B: To provide nutrients to the outer skin layer
options.C: To transmit electrical impulses to muscles
options.D: To filter waste products from the blood

explanation: Correct! This fluid acts like a natural lubricant, letting busy organs like your heart and lungs glide smoothly as they move. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: In a feedback loop, what is the component that senses changes in the internal environment?
explanation: You got it! The receptor acts as the body's lookout sensor, spotting changes and reporting them to the control center. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: How does a negative feedback mechanism respond when your body conditions drift away from normal?

options.A: It works to reverse the initial change and restore stability
options.B: It ignores minor shifts until organ damage occurs
options.C: It completely shuts down all metabolic activity in tissues
options.D: It amplifies the original stimulus to speed up the reaction

explanation: Spot on! Negative feedback is your body's thermostat—it counteracts shifts to bring things right back to a healthy, stable balance. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)
